## Plan for AsParallel() Misuse Analyzer Creating a new analyzer to detect incorrect usage of `AsParallel()` in LINQ queries. ### Problem - `AsParallel()` at the end of a LINQ query directly in a `foreach` is a no-op - Example: `foreach (var item in src.Select(...).Where(...).AsParallel()) { }` does NOT parallelize the foreach - Example: `foreach (var item in src.AsParallel()) { }` also does NOT parallelize the foreach ### Implementation Complete ✅ - [x] Explore existing analyzer structure and resource files - [x] Create new diagnostic rule CA1876 - [x] Create analyzer to detect `foreach` over `AsParallel()` result - [x] Add resource strings for the diagnostic - [x] Create comprehensive unit tests (11 tests, all passing) - [x] Build and test the analyzer - [x] Run dotnet format on changes - [x] Address code review feedback - [x] Revert unintended formatting changes (479 files) - [x] Regenerate auto-generated documentation files - [x] Convert test strings to raw string literals ### Changes Made 1. **New Analyzer**: `DoNotUseAsParallelInForEachLoop.cs` - Detects when `AsParallel()` is called directly in a foreach loop - Rule ID: CA1876 - Category: Performance - Severity: Info (IdeSuggestion) - Uses `SymbolEqualityComparer.Default` for proper symbol comparison 2. **Resource Strings**: Added to `MicrosoftNetCoreAnalyzersResources.resx` - Title: "Do not use 'AsParallel' in 'foreach'" - Message: "Using 'AsParallel()' directly in a 'foreach' loop has no effect and the loop is not parallelized" - Description explains the issue and suggests alternatives 3. **Configuration Files Updated**: - `WellKnownTypeNames.cs`: Added SystemLinqParallelEnumerable - `DiagnosticCategoryAndIdRanges.txt`: Extended Performance range to CA1876 - `AnalyzerReleases.Unshipped.md`: Added CA1876 entry 4. **Auto-generated Documentation**: - Regenerated `.md` and `.sarif` files using `msbuild /t:pack` 5. **Test Coverage**: 11 comprehensive tests covering: - Basic AsParallel in foreach (C# and VB) - AsParallel with LINQ chains (Select, Where) - Valid usage patterns (AsParallel with ToList/ToArray) - No false positives for regular foreach loops - **Updated**: All test strings now use raw string literals (""") for better code maintainability All tests passing ✓ Build succeeds without warnings ✓
Original prompt > > ---- > > *This section details on the original issue you should resolve* > > Use AsParallel() correctly > Using `.AsParallel()` at the end of a LINQ query, e.g. `foreach (var item in src.Select(...).Where(...).AsParallel(...))`, is a nop and should either be removed or the `AsParallel()` moved earlier in the query. I've even seen developers write `foreach (var item in src.AsParallel())` thinking it parallelizes the `foreach` loop, which it doesn't... it'd be good to warn about such misuse. > > **Category**: Performance > > Please create an analyzer in the net analyzers project that flags AsParallel() being used incorrectly, in particular when its result is directly foreach'd over. In such cases, it's a nop. You don't need to create a fixer for the analyzer right now, we'll start just with the analyzer. The details about the misuse can highlight that if it's used in a LINQ query, the developer should consider moving the AsParallel earlier in the sequence, or the developer might instead consider using Parallel.ForEach. > > ## Comments on the Issue (you are @copilot in this section) > > > @stephentoub > Here's an example of the kinds of things we'd like to catch: > https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/10937 > @jeffhandley > Estimates: > * Analyzer: Medium > * Fixer: Medium > @stephentoub > > guess the analyzer only triggers when the AsParallel is directly inside a foreach > > Yes > > > can only be resolved by removing the code. I guess that is the intended fix > > That's the safe fix, in that it doesn't change the semantics. It'd be fine to offer multiple fixes, though, with a second option being to move the call to the beginning of the chain, and if the developer chooses that, it's their choice. > @jeffhandley > @carlossanlop @buyaa-n Can you follow up with @Mrnikbobjeff on this? We would need to bring this in for API Review if we want to move it forward. > @stephentoub > > I do not think that would be advisable > > If someone added the AsParallel(), they intended for something to be run in parallel. And while we can't know for sure how much of the query that comes before it was intended, as an option I think it's reasonable to offer to fix it with our best guess for where it would go, which is at the beginning. The only 100% safe fix is to remove it, but both can be offered, and if we have any control which is the "default" / first option, it should be the removal. > @eiriktsarpalis > Hey @Mrnikbobjeff, would you still be interested in picking this up? > @ > Tagging subscribers to this area: @tarekgh, @dotnet/area-system-linq-parallel > See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed. >
> Issue Details >

I've even seen developers write `foreach (var item in src.AsParallel())` thinking it parallelizes the `foreach` loop, which it doesn't... it'd be good to warn about such misuse. > > **Category**: Performance > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
